$comment: Design-context artifacts that are NOT app-implementable primitives. The guard (bin/guard.py) detects these by signature and EXCLUDES them — they never reach map_all/synthesize, so the building agent cannot draw them. Mirror of real designs (e.g. Atlet's <div class=\"statusbar\">9:41 + battery + signal).
purpose: Distinguish design-context artifacts (OS chrome, device frame, annotations) from buildable primitives. Context artifacts are audited in breakdown.exclusions[] and dropped — never built.
overrideNote: A node carrying data-appbox="implement" is kept regardless of signature (designer asserts it is a genuine custom element, e.g. an app that truly custom-draws its status bar).
detectionNote: class/id/attr patterns trigger directly. text patterns trigger ONLY with corroboration (a text marker like battery/signal/wifi) to avoid false positives on legit in-app clocks.

kinds.label: OS / device chrome
kinds.reason: System-managed UI — status bar, home indicator, dynamic island, notch. The OS owns this; the app must NOT draw it. (e.g. Atlet's <div class="statusbar"> leaked into the build.)

kinds.label: Device frame / bezel
kinds.reason: Phone bezel, hardware buttons, device rounded corners drawn around the screen — presentation context, not app UI.

kinds.label: Design annotation / scaffold
kinds.reason: Figma labels, redlines, spacing rulers, component-name tags, grid overlays, comments — documentation overlaid on the design, not UI to build.

kinds.label: Browser / viewport chrome
kinds.reason: Address bar, tab strip — browser-owned on web targets; not part of the app surface.

kinds.label: Design-time tooling / tweak panel
kinds.reason: Authoring tooling used to iterate the DESIGN (accent/font/theme controls, EDITMODE inspector) — not shipped UI. e.g. Atlet's <TweaksPanel> is driven by tweakState/tweakOpen and mutates design variables; its controls (accent row, font segmented, switches) must never be built. Whole subtree excluded.
